items.title: Stepanov determinant
items.summary: On the proof path, `UpperTheory.TNZ.step_detVec` (depth 17) formalizes a 'determinant vector' property for representations twisted by determinant characters, which is part of the broader automorphic machinery but does not directly encode Stepanov's divisor-with-multiplicity argument. The more literal 'StepDet' namespace (in DivisorProofs and SatakeParameters modules) formalizes flag-determinant and step-determinant constructions off the proof path, suggesting the original Stepanov determinant concept was explored but not incorporated into the final proof.

evidence.name: UpperTheory.TNZ.step_detVec
evidence.shows: States DeterminantVectorProp: that twisting a spherical representation by a determinant character produces a 'determinant vector', and untwisting recovers sphericality. On the proof path, possibly a descendant of the Stepanov determinant idea recast in automorphic terms, but the mathematical content (representation twists, spherical vectors) is not the divisor-with-multiplicity construction described in the note.

evidence.name: UpperTheory.TNZ.DeterminantVector.hasDetVec_twist
evidence.shows: If a GL(N) representation ρ is spherical, then twisting by det∘η produces a representation with a 'determinant vector' for η. Part of the on-path determinant machinery.

items.title: Invariant derivation on a CM curve
items.summary: No formalization of D^p = 0 on a CM curve for p inert, nor of the divisibility estimate D^a theta(0)/Omega^a divisible by p^(a/p + a/p^3 + ... - O(log a)), was found anywhere in the archive. The ComplexMultiplication.Differential and FrobeniusAtPrimesLocal modules exist but are off the proof path and do not contain these specific statements. Extensive grep searches for iterated derivations, p-adic valuations of theta periods, and inert-prime derivation vanishing returned nothing matching.

items.title: qN = M^k + R sign argument
items.summary: The qN = M^k + R identity using the path quadric, Bertini sign argument from middle cohomology, and iterated Parseval bound is not formalized in the archive's proof path. While 'Bertini' appears in several off-path modules (e.g., Development.EtaleCohomology.WeilConjectures.FermatCount and Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Definitions.Divisors), and GL5 references exist, none of these are on the proof path and none match the specific 'sign-only proof of Weil and Deligne' structure described in the note. The concept appears to be part of an earlier conceptual timeline (10/19/26+) that was superseded by the iterated theta lift approach.

items.title: W(1_S) >= 0 via a determinant; bootstrap
items.summary: Neither 'bootstrap' nor 'Stepanov' appear anywhere in the archive. The Weil-type functional Formalism.G is defined but no positivity-via-determinant result for it (or any W evaluated at an indicator 1_S) was found, either on the proof path or off it. General determinant nonnegativity lemmas exist but are standard linear algebra, not the specific 'Stepanov with multiplicity one; bootstrap' idea described in the note.

items.title: Switch to the von Mangoldt sum; Guinand-Weil sign
items.summary: The defining function G(y) = Σ_{n≤y} Λ(n)·(y/n−1)_+ − y(log y − 1 − γ), which equals Σ_{n≤X} Λ(n)(X/n−1)_+ − X log X + (1+γ)X from the note, is defined verbatim as `Formalism.MainNotions.GlobalTheoryTheory.G` at depth 28 on the proof path. The same module also defines `sumLamChi` and `gChi`, the twisted versions over Dirichlet characters, which correspond to the "Mehta-like integral over twists" part of T05. The Guinand-Weil sign aspect is embedded in how these quantities enter the positivity argument (`W(1_S) ≥ 0`) used elsewhere in the proof.

evidence.name: Formalism.MainNotions.GlobalTheoryTheory.G
evidence.shows: Defines G(y) := (Σ n ∈ [1,⌊y⌋] vonMangoldt(n) · max(y/n−1, 0)) − y·(log y − 1 − γ), which is exactly sum_{n≤X} Λ(n)(X/n−1)_+ − X log X + (1+γ)X from the note.

evidence.name: Formalism.MainNotions.GlobalTheoryTheory.abelian₂
evidence.shows: Alias for the von Mangoldt function: abelian₂ n = ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt n, confirming the switch to Λ stated in T05.

evidence.name: Formalism.MainNotions.GlobalTheoryTheory.sumLamChi
evidence.shows: Twisted version: Σ_{n≤y} Λ(n)·χ(n)·(y/n−1)_+, generalizing G to Dirichlet characters; corresponds to the 'twists' aspect of T05.

evidence.name: Formalism.MainNotions.GlobalTheoryTheory.gChi
evidence.shows: Combined object: for χ=1 returns G(y), for χ≠1 returns sumLamChi(χ,y) + y·(L'/L)(1,χ); unifies the trivial and twisted sums in one definition used by the proof.

items.title: W(1_(0,1] + X^eta 1_(0,1/X]) >= 0 gives > 1 - eta
items.summary: The idea of obtaining a zero-free region from a positivity condition involving an X^η window is formalized as `zeroFree_of_rpow_window` in the module `Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.DedekindLFunctions.LandauTheorems.ZeroFreeOfRpowWindow`, taking θ ∈ (0,1) and δ > 0 and deriving zero-freeness for a CharFamily. However, this theorem is NOT on the proof path (depth None). The actual proof of RH uses `zeroFreeAll_of_topG` (depth 3) through a different mechanism involving `HostExW` and `TopG`.

evidence.name: zeroFree_of_rpow_window
evidence.shows: Given a CharFamily F, 0 < θ < 1, δ > 0, derives a zero-free region. Matches the note's 'W(1_(0,1] + X^η 1_(0,1/X]) ≥ 0 gives > 1 - η' — an rpow window positivity argument yielding a zero-free region parameterized by θ (= η).

items.title: Lower bound on divisibility of the m-fold lift
items.summary: The theorem `GlobalTheory.T.exists_primePow_dvd_mod_eisenstein_of_theta` (depth 18) and its proof companion `GlobalTheory.LiftDiv.dvd_mod_E` (depth 19) in module `Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs.InertiaEigenvalues.ExistsPrimePowDvdModEisensteinOfTheta` formalize the sufficient lower bound on divisibility of the m-fold iterated lift. The statement says: if the theta function evaluation at a lift element equals l^n times some element, then the lift element itself decomposes as l^n times a residual element plus an Eisenstein term — establishing the prime-power divisibility lower bound for the theta lift. Both declarations are on the proof path.

evidence.name: GlobalTheory.T.exists_primePow_dvd_mod_eisenstein_of_theta
evidence.shows: For a prime l, a BK (lift) structure bk over a field extension K, and an element s of the lift, if the theta evaluation Per.θ l (bk.ev s) = l^n * y, then there exist s', t such that s = l^n * s' + bk.E * t. This is the sufficient lower bound: theta divisibility implies lift element divisibility modulo Eisenstein, capturing T10's 'sufficient lower bound on divisibility of the m-fold iterated lift'.

evidence.name: GlobalTheory.LiftDiv.dvd_mod_E
evidence.shows: The proof of the same divisibility statement via p-adic norm estimates on the lift, confirming the prime power divisibility. The namespace GlobalTheory.LiftDiv ('Lift Divisibility') directly encodes the concept of divisibility of a theta lift.

items.correction: Sonnet said FOUND. Downgraded on manual check: the lemma is a divisibility statement (l^n | theta(s) implies s = 0 mod (l^n, E)), but nothing ties it to the m-fold lift.

items.title: Iwasawa tower via pigeonhole
items.summary: The Iwasawa tower (cyclotomic Z_l-extension) is formalized via the sequence of Galois subgroups `levU l U n` for n : ℕ, with fields K(ζ_{l^n}) giving successive levels. The theorem `exists_iwasawaRank_bound_of_ferreroWashington` applies the Ferrero-Washington theorem to produce a uniform Iwasawa rank bound `r` across all tower levels (`∀ n, XRk l 1 (levU l U n) r`), mirroring the pigeonhole principle on F_{q^n}/F_q (finite extensions of finite fields have bounded cohomology rank). This is used at depth 20 on the proof path.

evidence.name: UpperTheory.V.Ws.exists_iwasawaRank_bound_of_ferreroWashington
evidence.shows: Given the Ferrero-Washington theorem and an open abelian subgroup U of the absolute Galois group of Q contained in the kernel of the l-cyclotomic character, there exists a uniform Iwasawa rank bound r such that for all n, the Iwasawa rank of levU l U n (the n-th level of the cyclotomic Z_l-tower built from U) is at most r. This is exactly the Iwasawa tower (cyclotomic Z_l-extension) with uniform rank bound, the number-field analogue of the pigeonhole on F_{q^n}/F_q.

evidence.name: UpperTheory.V.Ws.rank_cocycleSpaces_le_of_towerIwasawaRank
evidence.shows: Given a Tower D with a uniform Iwasawa rank bound r, bounds the ranks of the cocycle and Str spaces at the base level, using the tower structure to propagate cohomological bounds. This is the downstream application of the Iwasawa tower rank bound.

items.title: Bost slope inequality
items.summary: The Arakelov slope formalism (definitions of normalized slopes muDef, muMaxDef, muMinDef over Hermitian lattices on number fields) is on the proof path at depth 23-25 in Formalism.HarderNarasimhan.StatementPl. However, the actual Bost slope inequality theorems (slopeInequality, SizeIneq, etc.) are all formalized in Development.AbelianVarietyTheory but NOT on the proof path. The definitions set the stage but the inequality itself is not invoked by the main theorem's dependency chain.

evidence.name: Formalism.HN.muDef
evidence.shows: Defines the normalized Arakelov slope mu(L) = 2*slope(L) - log 2 + logDisc(K)/[K:Q] for a submodule L of a Hermitian lattice over a number field K. This is Bost's slope in Arakelov geometry.

evidence.name: Formalism.HN.slope
evidence.shows: Defines the base slope of a submodule via the Harder-Narasimhan formalism, underlying muDef.

evidence.name: Formalism.HN.logDisc

items.title: Integral structure across Hecke characters (gcd)
items.summary: The IntegralStructures.ZetaCharacterDivisibility namespace contains on-proof-path machinery (depth 8-12) about extracting 'divisor' Galois representations compatible with automorphic representations across all places—conceptually a 'gcd' of integral structures. However, the specific idea of gluing across Hecke characters for extra averaging is not explicitly identifiable as a single declaration. Off-path declarations like exists_common_sublattice are closer in spirit but unused.

evidence.name: UpperTheory.Gal.Int.Div.DivAll

evidence.name: UpperTheory.Gal.Int.Div.IsDivRep
evidence.shows: Defines what it means for a Galois representation r to be a 'divisor representation': continuous, semisimple, and at almost all places its Frobenius eigenvalues match the algebraic Satake parameters of the automorphic representation U.

items.title: Normalized Gauss sum on the |mu_K|-fold cover of GL2
items.summary: The specific construction of a normalized Gauss sum of order #|mu_K| on the #|mu_K|-fold cover of GL2, with the reciprocity law giving a complete graph simplified to a path quadric, is not formalized anywhere in the archive. The archive has a local Gauss sum (gaussSumAt) on the proof path for Hecke epsilon factors, and metaplectic representation code off the proof path, but neither matches this concept.
